newsitem.title: USA: Sensormatic expects Q1 loss, lower sales.
newsitem.headline: Sensormatic expects Q1 loss, lower sales.

text.p: Sensormatic Electronics Corp said Wednesday it expects lower sales in the first quarter of 1997 compared with the prior year's first quarter, projecting a loss of between $0.05 per share and $0.10 per share.
The company said it expects sales in the range of $230 million to $240 million for the quarter, compared with sales of $267 million a year before.
Sensormatic, a supplier of electronics security systems, attributed the decline to shortages in key components and products needed for certain product lines.

The company said the product shortages may also affect earnings in the second quarter of 1997, since historically that quarter's sales are heavier in the first half of the quarter as retailers focus on the holiday season, the company said.
The shortages were largely the result of manufacturing disruptions in Puerto Rico because of Hurricane Hortense, as well as more orders during that period than were anticipated.

The Puerto Rico facility, which accounts for about 60 percent of the company's production, was shut down for about seven days after the hurricane because of power outages and interrupted deliveries from vendors and subcontractors.
